newsitem.title: USA: Florida financing pool plans $29 million issue.
newsitem.headline: Florida financing pool plans $29 million issue.

text.p: The First Florida Financing Commission, a consortium of Florida municipalities, will issue about $29 million of non-ad valorem revenue bonds in April, the commission's financial adviser said Tuesday.

The commission plans to insure the negotiated issue, which will be sold through a syndicate including Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, Merrill Lynch & Co, Smith Barney Inc, Raymond James & Associates Inc and William R Hough & Co.
The commission was formed six years ago by Broward County and the cities of Hollywood, St. Petersburg, Boca Raton, Clearwater, Gainesville and Sarasota
"By coming together, they take advantage of the economies of scale on the cost of issuance. Their borrowing costs will be much less," said John Haylett, financial adviser to the commission.
The pool has issued nine issues totalling $412 since its formation, all of them insured.

"They each can design their own debt service. We work with each borrower and put everything together and come out with one issue by the commission. We know specifically what portion belongs to each city."
The participants vary with each issue, and only three municipalities have agreed so far to participate in the April sale.

Broward County will receive $18.6 million of bond proceeds, to be used mainly for jail improvements. St. Petersburg will receive $6.3 million for improvments to Tropicana Field, the arena formerly known as the Thunderdome.

Hollywood will get $4.2 million for improvements to its police station and city marina and to bring 19 parks and recreation recreation centers into compliance with the federal Americans with Disabiliites Act.
